newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power falls amid oversupply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power falls amid oversupply.

text.p: Spot power prices in the Northwest U.S. continued to fall amid abundant hydropower supplies, while Southwest prices held comparatively steady amid below-normal temperatures, traders said Thursday.
"Real-time prices (in the Northwest) are even lower. There is a lot of energy on offer," said a California trader.
In addition to the continued cold-snap in parts of southern California, Arizona and New Mexico, firm natural gas prices were also cited as helping to support power prices.
Traders noted transmission constraints put in place after regional power blackouts last summer have limited the availability of Northwest hydropower to Southwest buyers.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Friday was quoted $13.50-14.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $15.50-16.50.
Off-peak COB for Friday was slightly lower at $8.50-9.50.
Friday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was lower at $12.00-$13.00, while off-peak was at $7.00-8.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Friday was quoted $20.00-21.00, little changed from Thursday prices.
Off-peak PV for Friday was unchanged at $10.00-12.00 per MWh.
Friday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $21.00-22.00, with off-peak at $10.00-12.00.
